decision_conditions:
<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="line-height: normal;">The proposed development, in the
absence of a satisfactory Retail Impact Assessment, has failed to demonstrate
that it would not cause harm to the vitality and viability of existing town
centres within the surrounding area.&nbsp;The proposal is therefore contrary to
the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy SD7 of the London Plan
(2021), Policy DM35 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan
(2013) and policy LE1 G of the Harrow Local Plan 2021-2024
(Regulation 19 version), November 2024.<font face="Arial, sans-serif"><o:p></o:p></font></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="line-height: normal;">The proposed development fails to
provide an effective ecological buffer to the adjacent Borough Grade II local
Site of Importance for Nature Conservation.&nbsp; The proposed development
would therefore result in unacceptable harm to the neighbouring wildlife site,
contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), policy G6 of the
London Plan (2021), and policies DM 20 and DM 21 of the Harrow Development
Management Polices Local Plan (2013).<font face="Arial, sans-serif"><o:p></o:p></font></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="line-height: normal;">The proposed development, by reason
of the excessive carparking area and single storey building on site would fail
to optimise the development capacity of the site whereby resulting in an
inefficient use of land, contrary to the high quality design aspirations of the
National Planning Policy Framework (2024), policy D3 of The London Plan, policy
CS1 B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and policy DM1&nbsp; of the Harrow Development Management Policies
Local Plan (2013).&nbsp;<font face="Arial, sans-serif"><o:p></o:p></font></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="line-height: normal;">The proposal, by reason of the site
being located within a high risk surface water flood zone and the lack of a
comprehensive Flood Risk Assessment, including details of compensatory flood
storage , has failed to demonstrate that the proposed development would not
exacerbate the risk of flooding within the site or increase the risk and
consequences of flooding elsewhere, contrary to the National Planning Policy
Framework (2024), Policies SI12 and SI13 of The London Plan (2021), Core Policy
CS1.U of Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and Policies DM 9 and DM 10 of the Harrow
Development Management Polices Local Plan (2013).<font face="Arial, sans-serif"><o:p></o:p></font></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-align:justify;text-indent:0cm;line-height:
normal;mso-list:l0 level1 lfo1"><span style="font-family:&quot;Arial&quot;,sans-serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">The proposed retail development
would result in a town centre use in an out of centre location and the
submitted sequential test fails to adequately demonstrate that there are no
more sequentially preferable sites available or expected to become available
within a reasonable time period and that the proposed development could not
demonstrate flexibility to form part of any of the allocations within the sites
identified within the planning statement / sequential site assessment. <b>&nbsp;</b>The
proposal is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework
(2024), policies SD6, SD7 and SD8 of the London Plan (2021), policy CS1.L of
the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), policy DM35 of the Harrow Development
Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and policy LE1 G of the Harrow Local Plan
2021-2024 (Regulation 19 version), November 2024.<o:p></o:p></span></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-align:justify;text-indent:0cm;line-height:
normal;mso-list:l0 level1 lfo1"><span style="font-family:&quot;Arial&quot;,sans-serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">The proposed retail development does
not meet an identified need within the London Borough of Harrow in this
location&nbsp;and would result in the loss of a utilities infrastructure site. The
proposal fails to demonstrate suitable alternative uses for industry, logistics
and services to support London’s economic function, contrary to Policy E4 of
the London Plan (2021), Policy CS1.O of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), and
Policy DM31 of the Harrow Development Management Policies (2013).<o:p></o:p></span></p>
description:
The construction of
a new food retail store, comprising the erection of a part one and two storey
building of Class E(a) floorspace, including a warehouse, ancillary staff
facilities, access, car and cycle parking, landscaping and associated works
